q0_helper_short: Search your neighbourhood or enter a postal code to match your street:
q1_hint_a: Residents with vehicles in the program area pay permit fees, which fully cover program costs and reduce street parking by encouraging off-street driveway parking.
q1_hint_b: Since no fee is charged, more vehicles park on the street.
q1_option_a: Residents with vehicles in residential parking program areas pay permit fees that cover all program costs.
q1_option_b: Tax-payers cover program costs through property tax revenues.
q1_question: Who should pay for residential parking programs?
q2_hint_a: Limiting on-street parking permits reduces the number of vehicles parked on the street and encourages off-street or driveway parking.
q2_hint_b: Since no fee is charged, more vehicles park on the street.
q2_question: Should your neighbourhood limit the number of on-street parking permits residents can hold?
q3_hint_a: Since a fee is charged, fewer vehicles park on the street and more park in driveways.
q3_hint_b: Since parking is on a first-come, first-served basis, available spots fill up quickly and remaining vehicles park on the street.
q3_option_a: Specialized paid permits are required to access work/loading zones.
q3_option_b: No restrictions - commercial and trade vehicles have access and do not require paid permits.
q3_question: What restrictions should be placed on commercial and trade vehicles in residential areas?
q4_hint_a: Since no fee is charged, more vehicles park on the street.
q4_hint_b: Since no fee is charged, more vehicles park on the street.
q4_option_a: Visitors digitally register their vehicles, with enforcement conducted regularly.
q4_option_b: Visitor parking is on a first-come, first-served basis.
q4_question: How would you manage visitor parking in your neighbourhood?
q5_hint_a: Since a fee is charged, fewer vehicles park on the street and more park in driveways.
q5_hint_b: Since no fee is charged, more vehicles park on the street.
q5_option_a: Residents and visitors — through permit fees, guest pass sales and violation fines.
q5_question: Who should pay for residential parking enforcement?
q6_hint_a: Since a fee is charged, fewer vehicles park on the street and more park in driveways.
q6_hint_b: Since no fee is charged, more vehicles park on the street.
q6_option_a: Paid parking with time limits and frequent enforcement.
q6_option_b: Maintain free, unenforced parking for visitors.
q6_question: How would you manage parking near major traffic generators, like educational institutions and hospitals?
q7_hint_a: Since no fee is charged, more vehicles park on the street.
q7_hint_b: Since no fee is charged, more vehicles park on the street.
q7_option_a: Conduct strict eligibility and digital pass checks, plus regular enforcement.
q7_option_b: No active enforcement, relying on public courtesy to obey zone signage.
q7_question: How would you manage accessible parking zones during events?
q8_hint_a: Since a fee is charged, fewer vehicles park on the street and more park in driveways.
q8_hint_b: Without a fee, more vehicles park on the street. If a fee is charged, fewer vehicles park on the street and more residents park in their driveways.
q8_option_a: Allow neighbourhoods to opt into fee-based parking solutions.
q8_option_b: Apply one city-wide set of rules.
q8_question: How should parking rules respond to the individual needs of each neighbourhood?

sync_guide_step1_desc: Download the template using the Download Full CSV Template button, then open Google Sheets and select File → Import → Upload.
sync_guide_step2_desc: Modify any phrasing in the "On screen text" (or add a "Revised text") column. In Google Sheets, click the blue Share button (top-right) and ensure General access is set to "Anyone with the link can view".
sync_guide_step3_desc: Copy the URL from your browser address bar or click Copy link in the Share dialog, return here, paste it into the URL field, and click Save & Sync Now. The app will automatically convert and sync the text!
